summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, diabetes, bipolar disorder, and a history of pseudoseizures was readmitted for severe right-sided abdominal pain worsened by a fall, following a recent discharge. He reported inability to tolerate oral intake and had a seizure likely due to missed medications. Imaging and labs showed no acute abnormalities, with normal lipase and a clear chest X-ray. The hospital course focused on pain control with morphine and Dilaudid, initiation of pancreatic enzymes and omeprazole for exocrine insufficiency, and discontinuation of all antiepileptic drugs after video EEG showed no epileptiform activity, confirming pseudoseizures. His diabetes was managed with reduced-dose NPH insulin, and amitriptyline was started for neuropathic pain. He was advanced to a regular diet, pain was well controlled, and he was discharged home with medication changes and follow-up plans.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
